text.p: - Russia's efforts to implement its reform programme are impressive enough for IMF to go ahead with the next tranche of its $10 billion loan, says IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus.
- Russia and Belarus sign a document which has no trait of a real Union Treaty and is nothing more than a step forward towards closer cooperation.
- Russia had no alternative but to tighten its ties with Belarus in the face of NATO's eastwards expansion.
- The communists in the State Duma lower house of parliament hail the union agreement with Belarus and promise to ratify it as soon as possible.
- IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus will not sign a single document during his visit to Moscow and the fate of the next tranche of the IMF loan to Russia remains unclear.
- Russia and Belarus sign a union treaty.
- The shape of the union between Russia and Belarus remains vague.
